title: Third-party dashboard extensions (plugin manifests, slots, SDK, route override)
contract: A full dashboard plugin system: manifest schema, discovery search order, a loader with a 2s safety timeout, a component registry, a `PluginPage` renderer, 30 named slots across every page, a plugin SDK exposed on `window` before first render, nav positioning and built-in route override (a plugin can replace `/chat`), asset serving from `/dashboard-plugins/<name>/<file>`, an API runtime gate, and a sidebar visibility toggle — plus two shipped plugin pages, Kanban and Achievements (web-shell.plugin-* — 13 entries, plus web-shell.plugin-kanban and .plugin-achievements, plus per-page plugin-slot entries on all 10 pages).
governance: Would sit *beside* the kernel rather than behind it — a spoofable approval surface. That is the disqualifying reason.
historical_exclusion_reason: Third-party JavaScript running same-origin inside the cockpit can read every governed surface, forge an approval dialog and issue authenticated calls with the owner's token — it sits entirely outside the Action Kernel, which mediates backend effects and knows nothing about a script that lies about what the owner clicked. Hermes can afford it because its dashboard makes no trust claim; Nerva's whole proposition is that what you see on the approval screen is what will happen. Re-open path: a slot registry that renders server-validated declarative panel descriptors (data, not code), behind a default-off flag — which gets most of the extensibility without the same-origin script.
